title: Design and locally rehearse the P10.3 IFX cutover and rollback
goal: Produce an evidence-bound inactive V4 IFX cutover proposal, prove coexistence and rollback transitions locally, and stop before any remote mutation or production cutover.
acceptanceCriteria: P10.1, P10.2 and Windows-full records bind the same V4 Guards 1.1.4, IFX 0.4.2 and target commit without drift.
Checked-in and live GitHub workflow, default-branch and ruleset state are captured read-only and discrepancies stop the design.
Every V3 required context and Architecture Conformance detector family has an explicit coexistence and final owner with no silent deletion.
The inactive workflow specimen uses trusted-base execution, immutable inputs, least privilege, no secrets and an always-present aggregate verdict.
Local forward, coexistence, primary and rollback rehearsals pass with trigger negative controls and exact restoration order.
No live workflow, ruleset, required check, branch setting, release, activation, cutover or V3 retirement is changed.
risks: A candidate-controlled workflow could judge its own guard changes.
Replacing V3 contexts before V4 aggregate proof could create a protection gap.
The accepted IFX bundle is not yet a tracked remote-consumable immutable asset.
A rollback ordered incorrectly could remove the new guard before restoring the old required protection.
A documentation-only authorization could be misrepresented as remote activation authority.
decisions: Keep all 13 V3 contexts required throughout the proposed coexistence window.
Add at most one future V4 aggregate required context after a separate negative-control proof.
Use GET-only remote inventory in P10.3 and defer every GitHub write to a later exact Plan and authorization.
Require immutable publication of the accepted IFX bundle before any remote runner may consume it.
Rehearse transitions as a local state machine and preserve V3/V3_ifx for rollback.
Leave P10.GATE, activation, cutover and V3 retirement false at P10.3 design completion.
